summary: Today’s pulse tracks Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock, Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland, and ‘Six, seven, maybe more preventable deaths’: Queensland’s LNP faces reckoning over broken health system. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are health, arrested, and australian. In the background, Cigarettes on silver platters at Bondi ‘clean’ beauty business lip gloss launch referred for investigation and Australian neo-Nazis among far-right groups raising hundreds of thousands via global crowdfunding platform keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
headlines.description: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.

headlines.title: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
headlines.description: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone attack on the vessel.

headlines.title: ‘Six, seven, maybe more preventable deaths’: Queensland’s LNP faces reckoning over broken health system
headlines.description: A government in office for more than two years is finally forced to take responsibility and seemingly no longer able to blame its Labor predecessors It is no great revelation to observers of Queensland politics that Miles, still seemingly bruised from his election loss two years ago, has struggled to find his feet as opposition leader. Many wondered why he wanted to stay on after the party’s drubbing in 2024. Some of Labor’s factional whisperers were telling anyone who would listen that the former premier’s leadership would come to an end in the weeks before Christmas.

headlines.title: Cigarettes on silver platters at Bondi ‘clean’ beauty business lip gloss launch referred for investigation
headlines.description: Copini Beauty referred to New South Wales health regulators, while federal government says it is ‘deeply concerned’ Photos from an event held earlier in November at a venue in Bondi, Sydney show what appears to be loose cigarettes without health warnings on a tiered silver platter alongside a bowl of lip glosses.

headlines.title: Australian neo-Nazis among far-right groups raising hundreds of thousands via global crowdfunding platform
headlines.description: GiveSendGo has been accused of facilitating the financing of extremism, but the platform says it does not ‘condone racism, discrimination, hate speech, or violence of any kind’ Of the 68 Australian fundraisers on the site, the White Australia party has raised the fourth-highest amount of money with $200,000 for its high court battle to overturn its ban as a designated hate group .

headlines.title: Louisiana man charged with killing woman on hiking trail and murdering co-worker with crossbow
headlines.description: Jared Schurr arrested in Mississippi after Lizeht Rodriguez and Woodrow Scott died in otherwise unrelated killings A man recently strangled a woman to death whom he did not know along a hiking trail north of New Orleans – then killed his co-worker with a crossbow two days later before being arrested in Mississippi after a police chase, authorities allege. Jared Schurr, 36, faces counts of second-degree murder in the killings of Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, and Woodrow Scott, 37, on 11 and 13 November, respectively, investigators said on Saturday.

headlinePool.title: Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
headlinePool.description: The mayor of San Francisco is asking people in the city not to travel unless "absolutely essential." Meanwhile, a storm moving up the Eastern seaboard could also cause travel delays ahead of Thanksgiving.

headlinePool.title: Suffolk village votes to ‘leave the UK’ over plans to house asylum seekers nearby
headlinePool.description: Local MP says legitimate criticisms of asylum housing plans are being co-opted by opposition parties ‘stirring up racial discord’ Residents of a Suffolk village have voted to “leave the UK” in a referendum held in response to government plans to house 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former military base. Approximately 500 people in Barnham were eligible to take part in the symbolic vote on Saturday. There were 257 votes for independence, 16 against and one spoiled ballot.

headlinePool.title: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off violence
headlinePool.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.

headlinePool.title: Trump orders contractors to check with White House over any congressional inquiries
headlinePool.description: Anticipating flood of Democratic requests, US president issues executive order in attempt to stymie oversight efforts Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to an executive order issued late Friday. The companies must also coordinate with the White House and US agencies on “appropriate responses” to any such requests, the order says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns, their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

headlinePool.title: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid
headlinePool.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of FBI’s most wanted fugitives and evaded capture for more than a decade The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s top 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night. Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that triggered widespread panic in the city of Guasave.

headlinePool.title: Vance stops short of endorsing Trump’s claim that Iran was close to nuclear weapon
headlinePool.description: US vice-president says it’s not his place to second-guess the president, but refrains from endorsing Trump’s claim At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that it was essential for the US to go to war with the Islamic republic. In the White House briefing room, Trump was asked about reporting this week that he was unhappy with the US vice-president’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war.

headlinePool.title: Anthropic mathematician claims he used Claude to prove 19th-century Riemann hypothesis
headlinePool.description: Levent Alpöge says it took six weeks for him using the AI tool to solve the math problem involving prime numbers A mathematician at Anthropic is contending that the San Francisco -based artificial intelligence (AI) company’s software has helped crack one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics. Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.

headlinePool.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
headlinePool.description: Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’ Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections. Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

headlinePool.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
headlinePool.description: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.
